title: Electron UI ↔ native/helper engine integration (T-008)
content:
# N-007 — Electron UI ↔ native/helper engine integration (T-008)

**Date:** 2026-05-13
**Scope:** End-to-end integration contract between the Electron renderer, the Electron main process, and the v2 native/helper replay engine. Locks IPC transport, message envelope, method/event catalogue, helper supervision, renderer state model, settings/hotkeys/UX surface, diagnostics surface, packaging implications, and the absorption of Issues #1 / #3 / #4 into the v2 path.
**Status:** Design only. No code, no prototype.
**Builds on:** N-002 (sidecar decision: Rust helper primary, ffmpeg-helper fallback, JSON-RPC over UDS / named pipe), N-003 / T-004 (capture method+event surface, `CaptureSource` trait, region as composed mode, `capture.sessionReady` as explicit readiness, restore-token persistence), N-004 / T-005 (encoder backend matrix, `encoder.probeResult` / `selected` / `fallbackEngaged` / `runtimeError` / `backPressure`, Linux rule: HW for live, CPU for re-encode), N-005 / T-006 (rolling segment buffer, `ReplaySnapshot` as paths-not-bytes, `replay.recoverable_sessions`, `replay.snapshot_release`), N-006 / T-007 (export state machine, `export.queued` / `started` / `progress` / `stalled` / `completed` / `failed` / `cancelled` / `rejected`, `ExportOptions`).
**Out of scope:** any Rust code, any Electron code, any preload code, any IPC handler implementation, any settings store implementation, any UI layout pixel-pushing, any packaging change to `package.json` / `electron-builder.yml`, any tests, any release build.

---

## 1. Three tiers, two IPC boundaries

The v2 architecture has three processes and two distinct IPC boundaries. Frames live entirely below the lower boundary; Electron above the upper boundary never sees a pixel.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Renderer process (Chromium / Electron renderer)                    │
│  - React/HTML UI, settings surface, hotkey overlay, toasts         │
│  - Talks to: preload bridge ONLY (no Node, no fs, no net)          │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                ▲                              │
                │ contextBridge events         │ contextBridge invokes
                │ (window.coveApi.on*)         │ (window.coveApi.*)
                ▼                              ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Preload bridge (sandboxed, contextIsolated)                        │
│  - The ONLY API the renderer sees                                  │
│  - Pure thin wrapper over ipcRenderer.invoke / ipcRenderer.on      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                ▲                              │
                │ ipcMain → webContents.send   │ ipcMain.handle
                │ (typed channels)             │ (typed channels)
                ▼                              ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Main process (Electron main)                                       │
│  - Helper supervisor (spawn / monitor / restart / shutdown)        │
│  - JSON-RPC client over UDS (Linux/macOS) / named pipe (Windows)   │
│  - Settings store (electron-store equivalent)                      │
│  - Hotkey registration (globalShortcut)                            │
│  - Window lifecycle, menu, tray                                    │
│  - Renderer event fan-out                                          │
│  - DOES NOT touch frames, ffmpeg, pipewire, encoder, segments      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                ▲                              │
                │ JSON-RPC notifications       │ JSON-RPC requests
                │ (length-prefixed framing)    │ (length-prefixed framing)
                ▼                              ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Native/helper engine (Rust sidecar — N-002 primary)                │
│  - Owns: PipeWire capture (N-003), encoder backend matrix (N-004), │
│    rolling segment buffer (N-005), export/remux pipeline (N-006)   │
│  - Owns: D-Bus portal connection, pw_stream, EncoderBackend,       │
│    SegmentSink, ExportWorker, diagnostics rotation, pid.lock       │
│  - Single per-app instance. Multi-instance is structurally refused │
│    via `engine.lock` exclusive file lock at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Boundary A (renderer ↔ main):** Electron's standard `ipcMain.handle` / `ipcRenderer.invoke` for request/response, `webContents.send` for fan-out events. `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`. The preload bridge is the only surface the renderer is allowed to see.

**Boundary B (main ↔ helper):** length-prefixed JSON-RPC 2.0 over UDS on Linux/macOS, named pipe on Windows. The main process is the JSON-RPC client; the helper is the JSON-RPC server. Notifications flow either direction. Pixel data never crosses this boundary — only typed control messages, structured progress events, and diagnostics.

**Why two boundaries, not one (i.e., renderer directly to helper):**
1. Electron's renderer must stay sandboxed; it cannot open arbitrary UDS sockets.
2. The main process is the natural owner of helper lifecycle (spawn, monitor, restart).
3. Centralising hotkeys and settings in main lets the renderer be replaced without changing the helper contract.
4. Crash isolation is structural: a renderer crash does not orphan the helper; a helper crash does not crash the renderer.

---

## 2. Renderer-facing preload API (the only surface the UI sees)

Exposed via `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('coveApi', { … })`. Names are camelCase TypeScript; channels are dot-prefixed for clarity. The renderer sees ONLY this object — it has no `require`, no `process`, no `fs`.

### 2.1 Capture

```ts
window.coveApi.capture.listSources(): Promise<CaptureSourceDescriptor[]>
window.coveApi.capture.requestSession(opts: RequestSessionOpts): Promise<{ sessionId: string }>
window.coveApi.capture.startStream(sessionId: string): Promise<{ streamId: string }>
window.coveApi.capture.pauseStream(streamId: string): Promise<void>
window.coveApi.capture.resumeStream(streamId: string): Promise<void>
window.coveApi.capture.stopSession(sessionId: string): Promise<void>
window.coveApi.capture.setRegion(streamId: string, rect: Rect): Promise<void>
window.coveApi.capture.setFramerateHint(streamId: string, fps: number): Promise<void>
window.coveApi.capture.setCursorMode(streamId: string, mode: "hidden"|"embedded"|"metadata"): Promise<void>

window.coveApi.capture.onSessionReady(cb: (e: SessionReadyEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.capture.onFormatChanged(cb: (e: FormatChangedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.capture.onStreamPaused(cb: (e: StreamPausedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.capture.onStreamResumed(cb: (e: StreamResumedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.capture.onSessionLost(cb: (e: SessionLostEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.capture.onDiagnostics(cb: (e: CaptureDiagnosticsEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
```

### 2.2 Encoder

No request methods. The encoder is selected by the helper based on capture parameters (N-004). The renderer subscribes to status events only — the UI displays the selected backend and any fallback indicator, but does not choose the backend (auto/preference flows through settings, not a direct call).

```ts
window.coveApi.encoder.onProbeResult(cb: (e: EncoderProbeResultEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.encoder.onSelected(cb: (e: EncoderSelectedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.encoder.onFallbackEngaged(cb: (e: EncoderFallbackEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.encoder.onRuntimeError(cb: (e: EncoderRuntimeErrorEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.encoder.onBackPressure(cb: (e: EncoderBackPressureEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.encoder.onDiagnostics(cb: (e: EncoderDiagnosticsEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
```

### 2.3 Replay (rolling buffer + save)

```ts
window.coveApi.replay.save(durationSeconds: number): Promise<ReplaySnapshot>
window.coveApi.replay.snapshotRelease(snapshotId: string): Promise<void>
window.coveApi.replay.recoverableSessions(): Promise<RecoverableSession[]>
window.coveApi.replay.discardRecoveredSession(sessionId: string): Promise<void>
window.coveApi.replay.restoreRecoveredSession(sessionId: string): Promise<ReplaySnapshot>
```

`replay.save` is a sync-return method (≤ 250 ms + encoder fragment latency per N-005 §15). The renderer ALWAYS pairs it with either `replay.export_start` (the common path) or `replay.snapshotRelease` (rare; only if the user immediately discards). Holding a snapshot indefinitely is a leak — see §10.

### 2.4 Export

```ts
window.coveApi.replay.exportStart(snapshot: ReplaySnapshot, options: ExportOptions): Promise<{ exportId: string }>
window.coveApi.replay.exportCancel(exportId: string): Promise<void>

window.coveApi.export.onQueued(cb: (e: ExportQueuedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.export.onStarted(cb: (e: ExportStartedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.export.onProgress(cb: (e: ExportProgressEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.export.onStalled(cb: (e: ExportStalledEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.export.onCompleted(cb: (e: ExportCompletedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.export.onFailed(cb: (e: ExportFailedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.export.onCancelled(cb: (e: ExportCancelledEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.export.onRejected(cb: (e: ExportRejectedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
```

### 2.5 Engine lifecycle / health

```ts
window.coveApi.engine.status(): Promise<EngineStatus>           // { state, helperPid, helperVersion, uptimeMs, lastError? }
window.coveApi.engine.restart(): Promise<void>                  // user-triggered restart
window.coveApi.engine.openDiagnosticsFolder(): Promise<void>    // shell.openPath under the hood
window.coveApi.engine.copyDiagnosticsBundle(): Promise<string>  // returns path to zipped bundle
window.coveApi.engine.onStateChanged(cb: (e: EngineStateEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.engine.onCrashed(cb: (e: EngineCrashedEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
window.coveApi.engine.onLogLine(cb: (e: EngineLogLineEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn   // optional, gated by diagnostics verbosity
```

### 2.6 Settings

```ts
window.coveApi.settings.get(): Promise<Settings>
window.coveApi.settings.update(patch: Partial<Settings>): Promise<Settings>   // returns the merged state
window.coveApi.settings.reset(): Promise<Settings>
window.coveApi.settings.onChanged(cb: (s: Settings) => void): UnsubscribeFn
```

### 2.7 Hotkeys

```ts
window.coveApi.hotkeys.list(): Promise<HotkeyBinding[]>
window.coveApi.hotkeys.update(id: string, accelerator: string | null): Promise<HotkeyBinding[]>
window.coveApi.hotkeys.onTriggered(cb: (e: HotkeyTriggeredEvent) => void): UnsubscribeFn
```

### 2.8 Dependency / environment probes

```ts
window.coveApi.env.probe(): Promise<EnvProbeReport>  // returns presence of pipewire, xdg-desktop-portal, libx264, helper binary, etc.
window.coveApi.env.onProbeChanged(cb: (e: EnvProbeReport) => void): UnsubscribeFn
```

No other surface exists. The renderer cannot open files, spawn processes, read env vars, or touch the network. Anything not in this list is unreachable from the UI.

---

## 3. Renderer ↔ Main IPC channel layout (Boundary A)

Electron's `ipcMain.handle` for request/response; `webContents.send` for events. Channels are stable string literals (no dynamic channel names — that prevents typo-induced silent drops and lets a single dispatcher route everything).

### 3.1 Naming convention

```
invoke channels (renderer → main):   cove/<domain>/<verb>
event channels  (main → renderer):    cove/<domain>/<noun>
```

Examples:
- `cove/capture/requestSession` (invoke)
- `cove/capture/sessionReady` (event)
- `cove/replay/save` (invoke)
- `cove/export/progress` (event)
- `cove/engine/status` (invoke)
- `cove/engine/crashed` (event)

### 3.2 Envelope

Invoke request/response are typed values; Electron handles serialisation. Events carry `{ kind, ts_ns, payload }` where `kind` is the dotted channel name and `payload` is the typed payload. The wrapping `kind` lets a single shared event dispatcher in the renderer route to the right `coveApi.*.on*` listener without each listener registering a separate IPC channel.

### 3.3 Backpressure / drop policy

Event volume is bounded: capture diagnostics 1 Hz, encoder diagnostics 1 Hz, segment-buffer diagnostics 1 Hz (N-005 §14), export progress 1 Hz (N-006 §17). Total steady-state event rate in a recording session is ~5–10 Hz, plus state transitions. No backpressure needed at the renderer; Electron's IPC queue is more than sufficient.

If the renderer is unresponsive (devtools paused), main continues to forward events to the helper; nothing in the helper depends on the renderer consuming them. Helper-side diagnostics rotation (N-003 §14, N-004 §17, N-005 §14, N-006 §16) is the source of truth for triage.

### 3.4 Error mapping

Every `invoke` resolves with `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, details? } }`. Exceptions in main translate to `{ ok: false, error: { code: "internal-error", message } }`. The preload bridge unwraps and either returns `value` or throws an `Error` with the helper's `code` set as `error.code` on the thrown object. This means renderer code can do `try { … } catch (e) { if (e.code === "helper-unavailable") … }` — concise and typed.

---

## 4. Main ↔ Helper IPC transport (Boundary B)

Locked per N-002.

### 4.1 Transport

- **Linux/macOS:** UNIX domain socket at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cove-screen-recorder/engine.sock` (Linux) or `${TMPDIR}/cove-screen-recorder.<uid>.sock` (macOS fallback when `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is absent). Mode 0600.
- **Windows:** named pipe `\\.\pipe\cove-screen-recorder-<uid>` where `<uid>` is a per-user hash of `USERNAME + SID`. ACL restricted to the current user (`SE_KERNEL_OBJECT` with current-user-only DACL).

The helper opens the listener and writes its PID to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cove-screen-recorder/engine.pid` (Linux) / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cove-screen-recorder\engine.pid` (Windows). The main process reads the PID file, verifies the process is alive, then connects to the socket. This handshake prevents a stale socket from a dead helper from being mistaken for a live one.

### 4.2 Framing

Length-prefixed JSON-RPC 2.0:

```
[ 4 bytes big-endian length N ][ N bytes UTF-8 JSON-RPC message ]
```

A `Content-Length` HTTP-style header was rejected: 4-byte length prefix is simpler, deterministic, and matches every other length-prefixed IPC we've shipped.

Message size cap: 1 MiB per frame. Larger payloads (which should not exist — frames never cross this boundary) are refused with `error: { code: -32600 }` ("invalid request"). Diagnostics arrays carry only structured counters, never raw logs.

### 4.3 Method namespace

JSON-RPC `method` field uses dotted namespaces aligned with the helper subsystem owners:

- `capture.*` — owned by N-003 capture orchestrator.
- `encoder.*` — owned by N-004 encoder layer (no request methods; events only).
- `replay.*` — owned by N-005 segment buffer + N-006 export pipeline.
- `export.*` — owned by N-006 export pipeline (events only; export start/cancel live under `replay.*` for cohesion).
- `engine.*` — owned by T-008 supervisor surface (health, log level, version).

### 4.4 Notification vs request

- Requests carry `id` and expect a response (success or error).
- Notifications carry no `id` and never get a response. ALL event-shaped messages (`*.sessionReady`, `*.diagnostics`, `*.progress`, etc.) are notifications.
- Main → helper: only requests. Main never sends notifications to the helper.
- Helper → main: both requests (the helper can ask main for input on something — currently only `engine.userPromptRecovery` for the "we found a recoverable session" flow; see §10) and notifications.

### 4.5 Reconnect

If the socket closes while a request is in flight, main rejects all in-flight promises with `{ code: "helper-disconnected" }`, fans an `engine.crashed` event to the renderer, and enters the supervisor restart loop (§9). New requests are queued during restart and either succeed against the new helper or fail with `{ code: "helper-unavailable" }` if restart fails.

---

## 5. Full JSON-RPC method catalogue (Boundary B, main → helper)

This is the authoritative list for the helper's RPC server. Every method maps 1:1 to a preload API surface in §2.

### 5.1 capture.*

```
capture.listSources()                                      -> CaptureSourceDescriptor[]
capture.requestSession({ mode, options })                  -> { sessionId, restoreToken? }
capture.startStream({ sessionId })                         -> { streamId }
capture.pauseStream({ streamId })                          -> void
capture.resumeStream({ streamId })                         -> void
capture.stopSession({ sessionId })                         -> void
capture.setRegion({ streamId, rect })                      -> void
capture.setFramerateHint({ streamId, fps })                -> void
capture.setCursorMode({ streamId, mode })                  -> void
```

### 5.2 replay.*

```
replay.save({ durationSeconds })                           -> ReplaySnapshot
replay.snapshot_release({ snapshotId })                    -> void
replay.recoverable_sessions()                              -> RecoverableSession[]
replay.discard_recovered_session({ sessionId })            -> void
replay.restore_recovered_session({ sessionId })            -> ReplaySnapshot
replay.export_start({ snapshot, options })                 -> { exportId }
replay.export_cancel({ exportId })                         -> void
```

### 5.3 engine.*

```
engine.version()                                            -> { helperVersion, protocolVersion }
engine.health()                                             -> EngineHealth
engine.setLogLevel({ level })                               -> void   // "error"|"warn"|"info"|"debug"|"trace"
engine.shutdown({ deadlineMs })                             -> void   // graceful; helper exits after teardown
engine.diagnosticsBundlePath()                              -> string // returns path to the latest rotated diagnostics zip
```

No `encoder.*` or `export.*` request methods exist. Encoder selection is automatic per N-004; export submission goes through `replay.export_start` because the export takes a `ReplaySnapshot` and is conceptually a replay operation.

---

## 6. Full event catalogue (Boundary B, helper → main, fanned to renderer as §3.1 events)

```
// capture (N-003 §2)
capture.sessionReady       { sessionId, streamId, format, restoreToken?, compositorName }
capture.formatChanged      { streamId, oldFormat, newFormat }
capture.streamPaused       { streamId, reason }
capture.streamResumed      { streamId }
capture.sessionLost        { sessionId, streamId?, reason, details }
capture.diagnostics        { streamId, state, format, buffers, cadence, cursorMode, compositor, pipewire, lastNegotiationMs, uptimeMs }

// encoder (N-004 §16, §17)
encoder.probeResult        { backends: BackendProbe[] }
encoder.selected           { backend, codec, parameters, reasonForChoice }
encoder.fallbackEngaged    { reason, fromBackend, toBackend }   // "no-hw-vendor"|"probe-failed"|"shm-forced"|"negative-cache-hit"|"windows-amd-deferred"
encoder.runtimeError       { backend, reasonCode, details, diagnosticsPath }
encoder.backPressure       { backend, sustainedMs, droppedSinceLast }
encoder.diagnostics        { backend, state, framesIn, framesEncoded, framesDropped, encodeLatencyMs, bitrateObserved, vbvUnderruns, dmabufImports, shmCopyBytes, hwencRuntimeErrors }

// segment buffer (N-005 §14)
replay.segmentDiagnostics  { sessionDir, state, currentSegmentIndex, fragmentsReceived, segmentsCommitted, segmentsEvicted, segmentsPinned, bytesOnDisk, diskWriteLatencyMs, fsyncLatencyMs, renameLatencyMs, backPressureSustainedMs, partialSegmentRecovered, formatchangeSegments, bufferWindowSecondsObserved, bufferBytesPctOfCap }
replay.recoveryAvailable   { sessions: RecoverableSession[] }   // fired at engine boot if N-005 §11 finds any
replay.snapshotPinned      { snapshotId, sessionId, segmentsCount, bytesPinned }
replay.snapshotReleased    { snapshotId, ageMs }

// export (N-006 §17)
export.queued              { exportId, snapshotId, requestedDurationS }
export.started             { exportId, mode, plan: PlanReport, estDurationS, estOutputBytes }
export.progress            { exportId, stage, pct, bytesIn, bytesOut, samplesProcessed, samplesTotal, etaMs }
export.stalled             { exportId, stage, lastProgressMsAgo }
export.completed           { exportId, finalPath, bytes, sha256, durationS, mode, fpsObservedOut }
export.failed              { exportId, stage, reasonCode, details, diagnosticsPath }
export.cancelled           { exportId, stage, partialBytes }
export.rejected            { exportId, reason }   // "queue-full"

// engine (T-008 §9, §10)
engine.ready               { helperVersion, protocolVersion, pid, capabilities }
engine.shutdownStarted     { reason, deadlineMs }
engine.logLine             { level, ts_ns, target, message }   // only if log level set ≥ helper threshold
```

Exactly one terminal event per `exportId` (N-006 §17). Every `sessionLost` carries a `diagnostics_path` pointing to the per-session JSON dump (N-003 §14, N-004 §17, N-005 §14, N-006 §16) — same shape across all four subsystems so a single triage tool reads any of them.

---

## 7. Message type definitions (TypeScript / binding shapes)

The types are TypeScript-shaped on the renderer side, Serde-shaped (`#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]`) on the helper side. The two MUST stay in sync; the JSON wire format is the source of truth. Naming convention: helper emits `snake_case`, the main-process bridge re-keys to `camelCase` before forwarding to the renderer. This isolates the JS-side from any future helper-side renaming.

### 7.1 Capture

```ts
type CaptureMode = "monitor" | "window" | "region";
type CursorMode = "hidden" | "embedded" | "metadata";

interface Rect { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number; }

interface RequestSessionOpts {
  mode: CaptureMode;
  cursorMode: CursorMode;
  framerateHint?: number;
  region?: Rect;            // required if mode === "region"
  restoreToken?: string;    // helper-issued, persisted across launches
  persist: "transient" | "permanent";
}

interface CaptureSourceDescriptor {
  // NOTE per N-003 §2: this is NOT a real enumeration; it returns mode descriptors plus known restore tokens.
  modes: CaptureMode[];
  knownRestoreTokens: { token: string; label: string; lastUsedAt: number }[];
}

interface CaptureFormat {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  fpsNum: number;
  fpsDen: number;
  fourcc: string;           // "NV12" | "P010" | "XR24" | "AR24"
  modifier?: string;        // hex DRM modifier, e.g. "0x100000000000002"
  colorPrimaries?: string;  // "bt709" | "bt2020"
  transfer?: string;        // "bt709" | "pq" | "hlg"
  range?: "limited" | "full";
}

interface SessionReadyEvent {
  sessionId: string;
  streamId: string;
  format: CaptureFormat;
  restoreToken?: string;
  compositorName: string;
}
```

### 7.2 Replay snapshot (mirrors N-005 §8)

```ts
interface ReplaySnapshot {
  snapshotId: string;
  sessionId: string;
  initSegmentPath: string;
  initSegmentBytes: number;
  segments: SegmentRef[];
  trimStartPts90k: number;
  trimEndPts90k: number;
  codec: "h264" | "hevc";
  timescale: number;        // always 90000 in v2.0.0
  width: number;
  height: number;
  framerateHint: number;
  hasDiscontinuity: boolean;
  discontinuityAtPts90k: number[];
}

interface SegmentRef {
  index: number;
  path: string;
  ptsStart90k: number;
  ptsEnd90k: number;
  duration90k: number;
  byteSize: number;
  isKeyframeFirst: boolean;
  discontinuity: boolean;
  fragmentCount: number;
}

interface RecoverableSession {
  sessionId: string;
  startedAt: number;        // unix ms
  durationS: number;
  bytesOnDisk: number;
  segmentsCount: number;
  hasDiscontinuity: boolean;
}
```

### 7.3 Export options (mirrors N-006 §19)

```ts
type AudioMode = "default" | "mute" | "passthrough";

interface ExportOptions {
  outputPath?: string;       // absent = use default dir + auto name
  maxCompat: boolean;
  audioMode: AudioMode;
}

interface PlanReport {
  mode: "fast" | "lead-reencode" | "discontinuity" | "full-reencode";
  copyRanges: { startPts90k: number; endPts90k: number }[];
  reencodeRanges: { startPts90k: number; endPts90k: number }[];
  estOutputBytes: number;
  estDurationS: number;
  expectedFps: number;
}
```

### 7.4 Engine health

```ts
type EngineState =
  | "booting"          // helper spawned, not yet ready
  | "ready"            // engine.ready received
  | "recording"        // at least one capture session active
  | "saving"           // a save in flight (snapshot pinned)
  | "exporting"        // at least one export EXECUTING / MUXING / VALIDATING / FINALIZING
  | "degraded"         // helper alive but reporting a runtime error
  | "restarting"       // supervisor restart in progress
  | "unavailable";     // helper failed to start or restart

interface EngineStatus {
  state: EngineState;
  helperPid?: number;
  helperVersion?: string;
  protocolVersion?: number;
  uptimeMs?: number;
  lastError?: { code: string; message: string; ts_ns: number };
  capabilities?: string[]; // e.g. ["capture.region", "encoder.nvenc", "encoder.vaapi", "export.full-reencode"]
}

interface EngineHealth {
  state: EngineState;
  uptimeMs: number;
  activeSessions: number;
  activeSnapshots: number;
  activeExports: number;
  lastErrorTs?: number;
  diagnosticsDir: string;
  rollingBufferBytes: number;
}
```

---

## 8. Renderer state model (FSM bound to events, not timers)

The renderer holds one explicit state machine for the recording session. Every transition is event-driven; no timer ever fires a state change. This is the structural answer at the UI side to the v1.1.x "freeze during save" and "timer says recording but capture not ready" classes of bug, and the absorption of Issues #3 and #4.

### 8.1 States

```
IDLE
 │ user opens source picker via capture.requestSession
 ▼
PICKING                     // user is in the portal dialog
 │ capture.requestSession resolves with sessionId
 ▼
SESSION_PENDING             // session created; stream not yet ready
 │ capture.startStream invoked
 ▼
STREAM_PENDING              // waiting for capture.sessionReady
 │ capture.sessionReady event ARRIVES   <-- the ONLY transition into RECORDING
 ▼
READY                       // green light; "Start replay buffer" enabled
 │ user toggles replay-buffer-active (settings has "start with replay on" toggle)
 ▼
RECORDING                   // capture flowing, encoder running, segment buffer rolling
 │ replay.save invoked
 ▼
SAVING                      // snapshot pinning; the UI is REACTIVE, not blocked
 │ replay.save resolves with ReplaySnapshot (≤ 250 ms + encoder fragment latency)
 ▼
SNAPSHOT_HELD               // snapshot in hand; user has 2 s to confirm export or discard
 │ user confirms export → replay.export_start                  user discards → replay.snapshotRelease
 ▼                                                              ▼
EXPORTING                                                       RECORDING
 │ export.queued / export.started / export.progress / export.stalled events drive substate
 │ terminal: export.completed | export.failed | export.cancelled | export.rejected
 ▼
RECORDING (continues during export; export is async)

Any state → SESSION_LOST   (on capture.sessionLost — UI offers re-pick)
Any state → ENGINE_DOWN    (on engine.crashed — UI offers restart)
```

Key invariants:

1. **`RECORDING` is reachable ONLY by `capture.sessionReady` event.** No timer, no `setTimeout`, no DOM mount, no preview hover, no probabilistic gate. This kills Issue #3 at the UI layer: there is no "capture might be ready, let's start the timer and find out." The timer in the recording HUD is driven by `sessionReady.ts_ns` from the helper, NOT by `Date.now()` on the renderer. Time-since-`sessionReady` is the only timer math allowed.

2. **`SAVING` does NOT block the recording HUD.** The HUD continues updating from `capture.diagnostics` / `encoder.diagnostics` / `replay.segmentDiagnostics` ticks during `SAVING`. The save spinner is its own component bound to the `replay.save` promise; the recording timer never freezes.

3. **`EXPORTING` is async and concurrent with `RECORDING`.** The export panel is a separate UI region (see §15) that lists active exports with their stage and progress; the main recording HUD continues unchanged. Cancelling an export does not affect recording.

4. **`SESSION_LOST` and `ENGINE_DOWN` are sticky.** They REQUIRE explicit user action (re-pick source / restart engine) to leave. They are not auto-recovered. This avoids spinning on portal-denied → re-request → portal-denied loops.

### 8.2 Substates inside `EXPORTING`

Each active export carries its own substate derived from `export.*` events:

```
QUEUED → STARTED → PROGRESS(stage = COPY|REENCODE_HEAD|REENCODE_BRIDGE|REENCODE_FULL|MUXING|VALIDATING|FINALIZING) → COMPLETED | FAILED | CANCELLED
                                                                                                                  ↑
                                                                                                                  └─ STALLED (transient overlay; not a terminal)
```

`STALLED` is a transient UI indicator that fades when the next `progress` event arrives. It does NOT auto-cancel.

### 8.3 Active session time vs replay window vs export progress

Three separate clocks; never conflated.

| Clock | Source | Display location |
| ----- | ------ | ---------------- |
| **Active session time** | `Date.now() − sessionReady.tsNs/1e6` (only valid in `RECORDING` and later) | recording HUD top-left |
| **Replay window duration** | Settings value (e.g. "last 60 s"). Static. | recording HUD, save button label |
| **Export progress** | `export.progress.pct` per export | export panel, per-row |

The v1.1.x "crop/replay timer weirdness" (Issue #4) is structurally absorbed: the timer is one calculation, sourced from one event timestamp, displayed in one place. There is no second timer in any sub-component, no DOM-mount-based reset, no MediaRecorder state subscription. The HUD timer reads `sessionReady.tsNs` at mount and updates every 250 ms from a single requestAnimationFrame loop; if `sessionReady` is null, the HUD shows "—:—" — not "00:00" — because there is no recording yet.

## 9. Helper lifecycle and supervision

The main process is the helper's parent and supervisor. It is the only writer to the helper's stdin and the only reader of the helper's stdout/stderr (which carry rotating diagnostics; the IPC socket carries control). One helper instance per app launch.

### 9.1 Launch sequence

1. On Electron `app.whenReady()`, before the first BrowserWindow is created, main calls `ensureHelperRunning()`.
2. `ensureHelperRunning()`:
   - Resolves the helper binary path: `process.resourcesPath/helper/cove-replay-engine[.exe]` in packaged builds; `${repoRoot}/target/debug/cove-replay-engine[.exe]` in dev (path read from `COVE_HELPER_PATH` env var if set, for local override).
   - Verifies the binary exists and the sha256 sidecar matches its computed sha256. If the sidecar is missing or mismatched, refuse to start and surface `engine.unavailable` with reason `helper-binary-tampered`. (Compliance with the global SHA-256 sidecar rule for releases.)
   - Calls `helperBinary --print-protocol-version`. If the value is incompatible with the protocol version baked into Electron, refuse with `helper-protocol-mismatch`.
   - Computes the socket path (§4.1) and the log directory (§16).
   - Reads `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cove-screen-recorder/engine.pid` (if present); if a process with that PID is alive AND owned by current user AND its `comm`/exe matches `cove-replay-engine`, treat it as ours and connect (this is the orphan recovery path; see §10.1). Otherwise unlink the PID file.
   - `child_process.spawn(helperBinary, ["--ipc-socket", socketPath, "--log-dir", logDir, "--log-level", currentLogLevel], { stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"], detached: false, windowsHide: true })`.
   - Wires stdout/stderr to the rotating log writer in the main process (§16). Optionally re-emits stderr lines as `engine.logLine` events to the renderer when `diagnosticsVerbosity >= debug`.
   - Polls `engine.version` over the socket with a 5-second timeout. On success, transitions `engine.state` to `ready` and emits `engine.ready` to the renderer.
3. If steps fail, transition to `engine.unavailable` and surface a modal to the renderer (§17.4).

### 9.2 Shutdown sequence

Three shutdown paths:

1. **Clean shutdown (user quits app).** Main sends `engine.shutdown({ deadlineMs: 5000 })`. Helper drains: stops every capture session, flushes the current segment to disk, finalises in-flight export VALIDATING/FINALIZING stages, releases pid.lock, exits with code 0. Main awaits exit up to 6000 ms; on timeout, sends SIGTERM; another 2000 ms; SIGKILL. Then unlinks the socket and PID files. Then `app.quit()` proceeds.
2. **Crash shutdown (helper exits unexpectedly).** Supervisor sees the child exit event with non-zero code or signal. Falls into §9.3.
3. **Forced shutdown (user clicks "Quit anyway" in an export-in-flight modal).** Main sends `engine.shutdown({ deadlineMs: 0 })`; helper SIGKILLs ffmpeg children and exits. Same cleanup of socket and PID files.

In all three paths, main scrubs `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cove-screen-recorder/engine.{sock,pid}` before app quit completes. This is the upper-layer carry-forward of v1.1.0's no-leftover-process invariant: any orphaned ffmpeg / pactl is a helper-side responsibility (N-006 §13 invariants make this true at the helper level), and any orphaned socket / PID file is a main-side responsibility.

### 9.3 Crash detection and restart

Detection signals (any one triggers restart consideration):
- `child.on("exit")` fires.
- The JSON-RPC socket reads 0 bytes (EOF) without a graceful `engine.shutdown` having been sent.
- A heartbeat (`engine.health` invoke) times out for 10 s while we believe the helper should be alive.

On detection:
1. Emit `engine.crashed { reason, exitCode?, signal?, stderrTail }` to the renderer. UI transitions to `ENGINE_DOWN` (§8.1).
2. Reject all in-flight RPC promises with `{ code: "helper-disconnected" }`. Reject all pinned snapshots in the renderer's hand (they are no longer valid; the helper's pin set is gone). UI clears `SNAPSHOT_HELD` and `EXPORTING` substates with appropriate failure events.
3. Run the supervisor restart loop:
   - Restart attempt 1: immediate.
   - Restart attempt 2: +2 s if attempt 1 fails within 5 s of boot.
   - Restart attempt 3: +10 s.
   - After 3 consecutive failures within 60 s, give up — emit `engine.unavailable` and STOP. User must invoke `engine.restart` manually.
4. On a successful restart, emit `engine.ready` and let the UI return to `IDLE`. **The renderer does NOT auto-resume the prior recording state.** A crash mid-recording is a clean cut; the user re-picks the source. This is intentional — silent auto-resume after a crash is how v1.1.x debugged into corner cases for an entire week.

### 9.4 Crash mid-export

If an export was EXECUTING / MUXING / VALIDATING / FINALIZING at the moment of helper crash:
- The temp file is left as an orphan (per N-006 §15).
- On next helper boot, the helper scans `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cove-screen-recorder/exports/manifest.jsonl`, unlinks any temp without an `ended` line, appends `outcome = orphan-cleaned`.
- The underlying snapshot's session may be recoverable; the helper emits `replay.recoveryAvailable` if so.
- The UI surfaces this as: "We found a recording from before the engine restarted. Save or discard?" (see §17.3).

### 9.5 Crash mid-capture

The rolling buffer for the in-flight session is recoverable per N-005 §11. The helper offers the recovered session via `replay.recoverable_sessions()`; the UI shows the same prompt as §9.4. The renderer never silently re-binds capture; the user explicitly chooses.

## 10. Orphan cleanup at app start and exit

Three classes of orphan:

### 10.1 Orphan helper process (previous Electron instance crashed but helper survived)

At main launch (§9.1), if the PID file exists and points to a live process named `cove-replay-engine` owned by the current user, **adopt it.** Connect to its socket; query `engine.version`; if compatible, treat as the live helper. This handles "Electron crashed; helper kept running" cleanly without a redundant kill+respawn.

If the PID file exists but the process is dead (or is a different command), unlink the PID file and the socket and proceed with normal spawn. If the PID file exists and points to a different user's process, refuse to start with `helper-pid-collision` — do not kill another user's process.

### 10.2 Orphan ffmpeg / pactl / pipewire-related children

The v1.1.0 fix for no-leftover processes is preserved by **moving the responsibility entirely into the helper**:
- The Rust sidecar spawns any ffmpeg subprocess with a known PID; on helper shutdown it sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL with bounded timeouts (N-006 §11, §13).
- On Linux, the helper sets `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL)` on each subprocess so any unexpected helper death cascades the kill.
- The helper does NOT spawn `pactl`. v1.1.0 used `pactl` for audio routing; v2 uses the PipeWire audio API directly (when audio lands; out of scope here) and never shells out to `pactl`. This eliminates the v1.1.0 leftover-pactl class entirely.
- On Windows, the helper uses Job Objects (`CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB = false`, `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE = true`) so child ffmpeg processes die with the helper.

The main process therefore only ever needs to kill ONE process (the helper). It does not chase ffmpeg PIDs directly.

### 10.3 Orphan files

On helper boot (helper-side, T-006 §11 already covers replay buffer dirs and N-006 §15 covers export temp files). Main does NOT scan these directories; it trusts the helper to clean them.

On main boot, main scrubs:
- A stale `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cove-screen-recorder/engine.sock` if the PID it pointed to is dead.
- A stale `engine.pid` file if its process is dead.
- A stale `lock` file in the settings dir (`electron-store` lock from a crashed prior instance).

## 11. Engine health / status polling

The renderer does **not** poll. The main process invokes `engine.health()` on a 5 s tick whenever no other RPC has come back from the helper in the last 5 s (i.e., a passive heartbeat that is suppressed when traffic is already flowing). The result is cached in main and exposed to the renderer via `coveApi.engine.status()`.

Health state is one of the `EngineState` values (§7.4). State transitions emit `engine.onStateChanged` events. The renderer subscribes once and re-renders the engine indicator (a small chip in the menu bar / status bar) whenever it changes.

The renderer should NOT call `engine.status()` on a timer. The event subscription is sufficient. Polling is reserved for app start when no event has yet arrived.

## 12. Settings surface

Settings live in `electron-store` (or equivalent) in the main process. The renderer never reads or writes the settings file directly. Schema:

```ts
interface Settings {
  replay: {
    durationSeconds: number;          // 10..1800; presets 30, 60, 120, 300, 600 surfaced; defaults to 60
    startReplayBufferOnLaunch: boolean;
  };
  capture: {
    mode: CaptureMode;                 // "monitor" | "window" | "region"
    region: Rect | null;               // valid only when mode === "region"
    framerateHint: number;             // advisory; 30 / 60 / 120 presets, custom allowed
    cursorMode: CursorMode;            // default "embedded"
    rememberRestoreToken: boolean;     // default true
  };
  encoder: {
    preference: "auto" | "nvenc" | "vaapi" | "qsv" | "libx264";  // hint only; helper may downgrade per N-004
  };
  export: {
    maxCompatibility: boolean;         // default false
    outputDir: string | null;          // null = OS default (see N-006 §8)
    overwritePolicy: "unique" | "prompt";  // default "unique" (auto -N suffix)
  };
  hotkeys: {
    saveReplay: string | null;         // default "CommandOrControl+Shift+R"; null = unbound
    toggleRecording: string | null;    // default "CommandOrControl+Shift+F9"; null = unbound
    pauseResume: string | null;        // default null
  };
  diagnostics: {
    verbosity: "error" | "warn" | "info" | "debug" | "trace";  // default "info"
    keepDiagnosticsBundles: number;    // count of rotated bundles to keep; default 5
  };
  startup: {
    autoLaunch: boolean;               // default false
    startMinimized: boolean;           // default false
  };
}
```

Main process behavior:
- A change to `replay.durationSeconds` is forwarded immediately to the helper via no RPC — durationSeconds is supplied per save call, so the helper is stateless on this. The setting affects the save button label and the value passed to `replay.save`.
- A change to `capture.mode` / `capture.region` / `capture.framerateHint` / `capture.cursorMode` while a session is active calls the corresponding `capture.set*` RPC immediately. If `capture.mode` itself changes, the active session is ended and the user is prompted to re-pick.
- A change to `encoder.preference` while a session is active is queued for the next session (the helper does not switch encoders mid-stream per N-004 §15).
- A change to `diagnostics.verbosity` is forwarded via `engine.setLogLevel`.
- A change to `hotkeys.*` re-registers the global shortcut immediately.
- A change to `startup.autoLaunch` calls `app.setLoginItemSettings`.

A change to `export.outputDir` to a directory the helper cannot write triggers a soft validation error on the next export, not at settings-save time (the helper is authoritative on permissions).

## 13. Hotkeys

Hotkeys are registered in main using `globalShortcut.register`. The list of bindable actions is fixed:

| Action | Default | Notes |
| ------ | ------- | ----- |
| `saveReplay` | `CommandOrControl+Shift+R` | Carries forward T-002 work. Triggers `replay.save(durationSeconds)` using the current setting; on success, immediately triggers `replay.export_start` with default options (or surfaces SNAPSHOT_HELD for 2 s if `confirmBeforeExport` is true — TBD as future setting). |
| `toggleRecording` | `CommandOrControl+Shift+F9` | Toggles the replay buffer on/off — invokes `capture.requestSession` + `capture.startStream` if off, `capture.stopSession` if on. |
| `pauseResume` | unbound | Invokes `capture.pauseStream` / `capture.resumeStream` on the active stream. |

When a hotkey is triggered:
1. Main fires the corresponding RPC.
2. Main also emits `hotkeys.triggered { id, accelerator, ts_ns }` to the renderer so the UI can show a brief on-screen toast ("Replay saved — exporting…").
3. If a hotkey fires while the renderer state machine would refuse the corresponding transition (e.g., `saveReplay` while in `IDLE`), main emits a `hotkeys.refused { id, reason }` event and shows a passive toast. The action is NOT silently queued.

Conflict detection: if the user binds an accelerator already registered by another app (the OS-level conflict — `globalShortcut.register` returns false on Linux/Windows; macOS does first-come-first-served), main emits `hotkeys.bindFailed { id, accelerator, reason }` and surfaces an inline error in settings.

## 14. Capture source / region selection UX (Issue #1 absorption — first-class)

This is the single biggest UX difference from v1.1.0. Region capture must NOT depend on the user guessing the portal's "Share region" path. The design:

### 14.1 Source picker entry

The primary entry is a single button: **"Pick source"**. Clicking it:
1. Reads `capture.mode` from settings. Default `monitor`.
2. Invokes `capture.requestSession({ mode, … })`. The portal dialog appears.
3. UI shows a passive overlay: "Choose a source in the system picker." There is no Electron-drawn picker.
4. On `capture.requestSession` resolve, transitions UI from `PICKING` to `SESSION_PENDING`.
5. On `capture.sessionReady`, transitions to `READY`.

The "Pick source" button is repeatable; picking a new source ends the current session and starts a new one.

### 14.2 Region mode (composed; N-003 §6)

When `capture.mode === "region"`:
1. The portal still shows a monitor picker. User picks a monitor.
2. After `capture.sessionReady`, the renderer shows a **region selector overlay** — a separate, frameless, click-through-elsewhere window that draws a darkened mask with a draggable selection rectangle over the picked monitor's geometry. This window is a renderer concern; it does NOT capture frames itself.
3. The user drags out a rectangle and confirms.
4. The rectangle is sent via `capture.setRegion({ streamId, rect })`. The helper applies the crop at the encoder boundary (N-003 §6) — no portal cooperation needed.
5. The user can re-open the region selector at any time via a status-bar button ("Adjust region"). It rehydrates the current rectangle and lets the user adjust without re-picking the portal source.

Visual states for the region selector overlay:
- **Before selection:** full monitor mask, no rectangle drawn, instructions overlay ("Drag to select region").
- **During selection:** rectangle being drawn, dimensions shown as `1280×720 @ (100, 100)`.
- **After selection:** rectangle shown with handles, "Confirm" / "Cancel" buttons.
- **Live adjustment (recording active):** same handles, change applies live via `capture.setRegion`.

Issue #1 absorption proof: the user never sees the phrase "Share region" from the portal. The region UX is owned entirely by the renderer + helper.

### 14.3 Restore tokens

If a known restore token exists for the chosen source (returned in `CaptureSourceDescriptor.knownRestoreTokens`), the picker entry shows it as a quick-pick row: **"Last used: Monitor 1 (DP-1)"**. Clicking invokes `capture.requestSession` with the stored token; the portal suppresses the dialog. Falls back gracefully if the token is rejected (per N-003 §5).

The "Forget all sources" action in settings clears the helper-side restore-token file.

## 15. Replay save / export UX

### 15.1 Save button

The save button label is **"Save last 60 s"** (substituting the configured replay duration). It is enabled only in `RECORDING`. Click:
1. Renderer invokes `coveApi.replay.save(durationSeconds)`.
2. While the promise is in flight (≤ 250 ms + encoder fragment latency), the button shows a spinner; the recording HUD timer continues ticking — no freeze.
3. On resolve with `ReplaySnapshot`, renderer either (a) invokes `replay.exportStart` immediately with default `ExportOptions`, or (b) — if `confirmBeforeExport` is true (future setting) — shows a brief modal with output path preview and a "Save" / "Discard" choice. For v2.0.0, default behaviour is (a) — the hotkey path is one-click.

### 15.2 Export panel

A collapsible panel docked to the bottom of the window lists every active export. Each row:
- File name (preview / final).
- Stage badge (`COPY`, `REENCODE_HEAD`, `MUXING`, etc.).
- Progress bar (`pct` from `export.progress`).
- ETA (`etaMs` formatted).
- Cancel button — DISABLED past `MUXING` (the rejection rule in N-006 §11). Tooltip on disabled: "Finalising — cannot cancel".
- Stall indicator overlay ("No progress for 12 s") when `export.stalled` arrives; clears on next `export.progress`.

On `export.completed`:
- Row collapses into a success state with the final file name.
- A toast appears: **"Replay saved — Replay-2026-05-13-141532-60s.mp4"** with a **"Show in folder"** button (invokes `shell.showItemInFolder` via the main process bridge).
- After 5 s, the row disappears from the active list and moves to a recent-exports history.

On `export.failed`:
- Row shows the reason (mapped per §17.1) and a **"Show diagnostics"** button that opens `diagnosticsPath` via `shell.showItemInFolder`.
- A toast appears: **"Export failed — codec mismatch in source"** (or similar mapped string).

On `export.cancelled`:
- Row disappears silently. A brief toast: "Export cancelled".

On `export.rejected`:
- A toast: **"Too many pending exports — please wait."** No row added.

### 15.3 Recoverable session prompt

On engine boot, if `replay.recoveryAvailable` arrives (N-005 §11 found a recoverable session), the renderer shows a non-modal banner at the top of the window: **"We found a recording from your last session (5 min 23 s, 250 MB). [Save] [Discard]"**.
- **Save** → invokes `replay.restoreRecoveredSession(sessionId)` → returns a `ReplaySnapshot` → renderer invokes `replay.exportStart` with default options → standard export flow.
- **Discard** → invokes `replay.discardRecoveredSession(sessionId)` → banner clears.

The banner is sticky until the user acts. If more than one recoverable session exists (rare; would require multiple crash-without-discard cycles), the banner stacks one row per session.

## 16. Diagnostics and logging surface

Three separate sinks; the user can reach any of them in two clicks.

### 16.1 Helper-side rotating diagnostics

Location: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cove-screen-recorder/diagnostics/` (Linux) / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cove-screen-recorder\diagnostics\` (Windows). Owned by the helper.

Contents (per N-003 §14, N-004 §17, N-005 §14, N-006 §16):
- Per-session JSON dumps written on `sessionLost` / `encoder.runtimeError` / fatal segment errors / export failures: `<sessionId>.json` or `<exportId>.json`.
- A rolling log file `engine.log` containing tracing output from the helper at the configured log level. Rotated at 50 MiB or 24 h, retained per `keepDiagnosticsBundles` setting.

The helper writes these files directly. Main does not.

### 16.2 Main-side log

Location: `app.getPath("logs")/main.log` (Electron's standard). Captures:
- Helper supervisor decisions (spawn, exit code, restart attempts).
- IPC connection / disconnection events.
- Settings changes.
- Hotkey registration outcomes.
- Renderer crashes (captured via `webContents.on("render-process-gone")`).

This log is the artifact a user attaches when the helper itself can't be reached.

### 16.3 Renderer-side console buffer (in-memory)

The renderer keeps the last 200 `engine.logLine` events in memory (when log level is `debug` or higher) and renders them in a developer pane reachable via Settings → Diagnostics → "View live engine log". This is for development convenience, not user-facing triage.

### 16.4 Diagnostics bundle

`coveApi.engine.copyDiagnosticsBundle()` produces a zip in the user's temp dir containing: the last N per-session JSON dumps, the helper log tail (last 10 MiB), the main log tail, the current settings (sensitive fields redacted: restore tokens, output paths), and an environment manifest (OS, kernel, PipeWire version, compositor name, GPU vendor/driver, helper version, Electron version). The settings panel surfaces a **"Copy diagnostics bundle"** button that returns the path.

### 16.5 Verbosity setting

`settings.diagnostics.verbosity` is forwarded to the helper via `engine.setLogLevel` on change. Default `info`. The user is encouraged to set `debug` only when reproducing a bug.

## 17. Error mapping (helper reason codes → user-facing messages)

The helper emits structured reason codes (N-003 §13, N-004 §18, N-005 §12, N-006 §14). The renderer maps them to a single user-facing string + optional CTA. The mapping is owned by the renderer; the helper does NOT format strings.

### 17.1 Capture / encoder / segment / export

| Reason code | User-facing message | CTA |
| ----------- | ------------------- | --- |
| `portal-denied` | (silent UI dismissal) | — |
| `portal-unavailable` | "Screen capture is not available on this system. Install xdg-desktop-portal." | "Open install guide" → opens docs URL |
| `source-removed` | "The source you were capturing is no longer available." | "Pick another source" |
| `pipewire-disconnected` | "PipeWire stopped responding. Reconnecting…" | (passive; auto-resolves) |
| `no-acceptable-buffer-type` | "This compositor can't produce a usable video stream. Check your graphics driver." | "Show diagnostics" |
| `encoder-probe-failed` | "No hardware encoder available — using CPU encoder (libx264)." | (informational; matched to fallback indicator chip) |
| `encoder-runtime-error` | "The hardware encoder hit an error. Switched to CPU encoder." | "Try again" / "Show diagnostics" |
| `encoder-fallback-engaged` (informational) | (status chip update; no modal) | — |
| `segment-sink-disk-full` | "Out of disk space — recording stopped." | "Open output folder" |
| `segment-sink-state-dir-unwritable` | "The recording folder is not writable." | "Choose another folder" → opens settings |
| `ffmpeg-spawn-failed` | "Could not start the export. Engine may be misconfigured." | "Show diagnostics" |
| `ffmpeg-exited-nonzero` | "Export failed." + helper detail tail | "Show diagnostics" |
| `reencode-libx264-missing` | "libx264 is missing — please reinstall the app." | "Show diagnostics" |
| `finalize-disk-full` | "Out of disk space — could not save the export." | "Open output folder" |
| `helper-disconnected` | "The engine stopped responding — restarting." | (passive; auto-resolves or surfaces unavailable) |
| `helper-unavailable` | "The engine could not start. Check diagnostics." | "Copy diagnostics bundle" / "Retry" |
| `helper-binary-tampered` | "The engine binary failed verification. Reinstall the app." | "Show download link" |
| `helper-protocol-mismatch` | "This engine version is incompatible. Reinstall the app." | "Show download link" |

The principle: every reason code maps to ONE message string and at most one CTA. No catch-all "unknown error" — if a code is not in the table, surface the code verbatim ("Engine error: foo-bar — please report this") so triage gets useful telemetry. Unrecognised codes are a defect to be filed.

### 17.2 Platform dependency probe surface

On app start, `coveApi.env.probe()` returns an `EnvProbeReport` enumerating the presence/version of:
- `xdg-desktop-portal` (Linux)
- `pipewire` (Linux)
- `libx264` (linked into helper or system; helper reports)
- `helper` binary itself (path, version, sha256 match)
- GPU vendor & driver version (informational)

If any required dependency is missing, the renderer shows a **modal blocking the main UI** with a list of missing items and per-item install hints (with platform-specific copy: "sudo apt install xdg-desktop-portal-wlr", or a link to a docs page). The app is not usable until the user dismisses or fixes the issue; settings remain reachable.

### 17.3 Recoverable session prompt

Covered in §15.3.

### 17.4 Engine unavailable modal

When `engine.state === "unavailable"`, the renderer overlays a centred modal: **"The engine could not start. [Retry] [Copy diagnostics bundle] [Quit]"**. The Retry button invokes `coveApi.engine.restart()`. The modal stays until restart succeeds or the user quits.

### 18.2 Issue #3 — source does not record until hovered

Absorbed in three layers:

1. **The helper produces frames as soon as `pw_stream` state reaches `Streaming` with a committed format** (N-003 §5). No DOM, no canvas, no `getDisplayMedia`, no preview-tile-must-be-visible coupling.
2. **`capture.sessionReady` is the ONLY transition into `RECORDING` in the renderer FSM** (§8.1). The UI cannot "think it's recording" before the helper confirms it is.
3. **The HUD timer reads `sessionReady.tsNs` from the event** (§8.3), not `Date.now()` at component mount. If the user minimizes the window the moment they hit Record, the timer still shows accurate elapsed time when they return because the timestamp is server-issued.

The N-003 §17 case 24 validation (60 s minimised-preview capture must produce the expected frame count) is the load-bearing assertion that v2 escapes the v1.1.0 ceiling at the UX layer too.

### 18.3 Issue #4 — crop/replay timer state weirdness

Absorbed by the FSM (§8.1) and the three-clocks rule (§8.3):

1. **`SAVING` is a real state distinct from `RECORDING`,** and the recording HUD timer continues updating from `capture.diagnostics` during `SAVING`. The v1.1.0 "timer froze during save" symptom is structurally impossible.
2. **The replay window duration is a static settings value,** never derived from elapsed time. "Save last 60 s" means 60 s, full stop.
3. **Export progress is its own clock** (§8.3) in its own panel (§15.2). It is never conflated with recording time.
4. **Region rectangle is a settings value forwarded via `capture.setRegion`.** It does not interact with the timer. Changing the region mid-recording does not pause, restart, or otherwise mutate the timer.

## 19. Packaging implications for electron-builder

These are notes for the eventual implementation ticket; they do not require any `package.json` / `electron-builder.yml` change in this design session.

- **Extra resources:** the helper binary is shipped as `extraResources` per target (`build.extraResources` block in `electron-builder.yml`). Path inside the asar/app: `resources/helper/cove-replay-engine[.exe]`. Single statically-linked Rust binary per target (N-002).
- **SHA-256 sidecar for the helper:** the helper binary gets a `cove-replay-engine.sha256` (or `.exe.sha256`) sidecar shipped alongside it in `extraResources`. Main verifies it at boot (§9.1). The release artifact build also produces `.sha256` sidecars per the global rule (`cove-screen-recorder-Setup.exe.sha256`, `cove-screen-recorder.AppImage.sha256`, etc.).
- **Build matrix:** Linux x86_64 (AppImage, .deb), Windows x86_64 (Portable.exe, Setup.exe). macOS deferred. Each target's helper is cross-compiled or built on-target (Rust supports both); we recommend on-target builds with `cargo` to avoid sysroot pain for libpipewire/libdrm linkage on Linux.
- **Code signing (Windows):** the helper executable should be signed in the same step as the Electron main exe so SmartScreen does not block it. Apple Developer ID signing of the helper is gated on macOS landing.
- **Linux runtime dependencies:** PipeWire (≥ 0.3.x) and xdg-desktop-portal (≥ 1.18 for restore tokens) are runtime requirements. The AppImage bundles libraries it can (libavcodec via static linkage in the helper); it cannot bundle PipeWire or the portal. The dependency probe (§17.2) surfaces missing ones with install hints.
- **Linux .deb dependencies:** the `.deb` declares Depends on `pipewire (>= 0.3.x)`, `xdg-desktop-portal (>= 1.18)`. We do not require a specific portal backend; the user picks (`xdg-desktop-portal-gnome`, `-kde`, `-wlr`).
- **Windows runtime dependencies:** none beyond the Visual C++ Redistributable bundled by electron-builder defaults. No PipeWire on Windows; the future `WgcSource` (N-003 §18) uses Windows.Graphics.Capture which is OS-bundled.
- **Auto-update:** unchanged from v1.1.0. The helper is replaced atomically along with the rest of the resources by the auto-updater. On next launch, the SHA-256 check (§9.1) covers integrity.
- **The helper is NOT installed system-wide.** It lives in the app's resource directory. Multiple Cove installs on the same machine each have their own helper.

## 20. Runtime dependency detection (Linux first; Windows path shape)

Linux:
- `xdg-desktop-portal` presence: probed via D-Bus name `org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop`. Absent → `helper-unavailable` with `portal-unavailable`.
- PipeWire presence: probed by attempting `pw_context_connect`. Absent → `helper-unavailable` with `pipewire-unavailable`.
- `libx264` presence: linked into the helper (statically by default; dynamically if the helper was built that way). The helper at probe time verifies x264 is callable. Absent → `helper-unavailable` with `libx264-missing`.
- GPU vendor detection: `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/vendor` (PCI) + `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` (NVIDIA proprietary). Surfaces as `EnvProbeReport.gpu` for informational display; does not block startup.
- Restore token storage probe: `$XDG_STATE_HOME` exists and is writable. Falls back to `~/.local/state` if `$XDG_STATE_HOME` is unset.

Windows (forward-looking path shape; not implemented in v2.0.0):
- Windows.Graphics.Capture availability: probed via `WinRT::Graphics::Capture::GraphicsCaptureSession::IsSupported`. Windows 10 1903+.
- D3D11 device creation: probed at helper boot.
- libx264 presence: same as Linux (statically linked).
- Auto-start (`startup.autoLaunch`): uses `app.setLoginItemSettings` which on Windows writes the `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` key.

The `EnvProbeReport` shape is platform-agnostic; only the keys present differ.

## 21. Linux-first behavior and Windows path shape

Linux is the primary v2.0.0 target. Everything in this design is implementable on Linux today.

Windows path shape is preserved in the design so that landing Windows later does not require re-shaping this contract:

- The IPC transport switch (UDS ↔ named pipe) is the only main-process change needed.
- The capture trait already accommodates `WgcSource` (N-003 §18).
- The encoder trait already accommodates `AmfEncoder` (N-004 §1, slot reserved; falls through to libx264 for v2.0.0).
- The packaging is symmetric (`extraResources` per target; sha256 sidecar per artifact).
- The settings schema (§12) and event surface (§6) are platform-agnostic.
- The renderer FSM (§8) is platform-agnostic.

Things that explicitly differ on Windows:
- Hotkey accelerator strings (e.g. `Cmd` → `Ctrl`). Electron's `Accelerator` string handles this transparently with `CommandOrControl`.
- Output dir default (`%USERPROFILE%\Videos\Cove Replays\` vs `$XDG_VIDEOS_DIR/Cove Replays/`).
- Diagnostics dir default (`%LOCALAPPDATA%` vs `$XDG_STATE_HOME`).
- Auto-launch mechanism (registry Run key vs `.desktop` autostart entry).

These differences are localised to settings defaults and path resolution; the rest of the contract is identical.

## 22. What T-009 must validate

This section feeds T-009 (validation matrix) directly with UI-layer cases. Combined with the helper-side cases enumerated in N-003 §17, N-004 §20, N-005 §19, N-006 §18, this completes the v2 validation surface.

**Lifecycle / supervision:**

1. App start with helper binary present and valid sha256: engine reaches `ready` within 2 s of `app.whenReady()`.
2. App start with sha256 mismatch: engine surfaces `helper-binary-tampered` modal; no helper spawned.
3. App start with protocol-version mismatch: engine surfaces `helper-protocol-mismatch` modal.
4. App start with helper PID file pointing to a live helper of the same version: main adopts the running helper; no respawn.
5. App start with helper PID file pointing to a dead PID: main unlinks PID + socket and respawns.
6. App start with helper PID file pointing to another user's process: main refuses with `helper-pid-collision`.
7. Kill the helper while idle (no session): main detects exit, attempts restart (immediate, +2 s, +10 s); after 3 failures emits `helper-unavailable`.
8. Kill the helper mid-recording: renderer transitions to `ENGINE_DOWN`; in-flight `replay.save` / `replay.exportStart` promises reject with `helper-disconnected`; on restart, renderer returns to `IDLE` (does NOT auto-resume).
9. Kill the helper mid-export: helper temp file is orphaned; next helper boot's manifest scan unlinks it; `replay.recoveryAvailable` may surface the source session.
10. Clean app quit: `engine.shutdown` fires; helper exits within 5 s; main scrubs socket and PID files; no orphan ffmpeg / pactl processes.

**Renderer FSM:**

11. `RECORDING` is reachable ONLY via `capture.sessionReady`. Mock the event delivery: `requestSession` resolves but `sessionReady` never arrives → renderer stays in `STREAM_PENDING`; HUD timer reads "—:—".
12. `SAVING` does not freeze the recording HUD: while a save is in flight, the HUD timer continues to update from `capture.diagnostics` ticks.
13. `EXPORTING` is concurrent with `RECORDING`: starting an export does not pause the recording HUD; cancelling an export does not affect the recording.
14. Two simultaneous exports: both rows appear in the export panel; both progress independently; cancelling one does not affect the other.
15. `SESSION_LOST` is sticky: receiving `capture.sessionLost` puts the UI in `SESSION_LOST` and only "Pick source" leaves it. Subsequent diagnostics events do not transition.

**Region UX (Issue #1):**

16. Pick `region` mode; portal returns a monitor; renderer shows region overlay; user draws rectangle; `capture.setRegion` is called with the exact rectangle; recording starts; the saved replay's video is the rectangle (verified by ffprobe dimensions).
17. Adjust region mid-recording: `capture.setRegion` is called; the saved replay's video reflects the new rectangle from the moment of the change; no `formatChanged` event (crop is a virtual change inside the encoder boundary).
18. Region rectangle outside monitor bounds: helper rejects with a structured error; renderer shows a soft inline error in the region overlay; recording state unchanged.

**Issue #3 absorption:**

19. Start a recording; minimise the Electron window for 60 s; verify the recording HUD's elapsed time on restore matches wall-clock elapsed; verify `capture.diagnostics.buffers.total_produced` increased by the expected frame count over the 60 s.
20. Start a recording with devtools paused on the renderer; verify the helper continues to emit fragments and the segment buffer continues to commit.

**Issue #4 absorption:**

21. Recording HUD timer reads `sessionReady.tsNs`-anchored elapsed time; no second timer source exists in the renderer code (grep test).
22. Replay window setting changes do not affect the running timer; only the save button label updates.
23. Three simultaneous clocks (active session time, replay window duration, export progress) render in three distinct UI regions with no shared state.

**Hotkeys:**

24. `saveReplay` hotkey while in `RECORDING`: invokes `replay.save` → `replay.exportStart`; toast appears within 250 ms; export panel populates.
25. `saveReplay` hotkey while in `IDLE`: refused with `hotkeys.refused` event and passive toast; no RPC fired.
26. Conflicting accelerator (already bound by another app): settings inline error displayed; binding rolled back.

**Dependency probe:**

27. xdg-desktop-portal missing: blocking modal with install hint.
28. PipeWire missing: blocking modal with install hint.
29. Helper binary missing: `helper-unavailable` modal with reinstall CTA.
30. Helper sha256 mismatch: `helper-binary-tampered` modal.

**Settings:**

31. Change replay duration mid-recording: save button label updates immediately; next save uses the new duration; no helper RPC fired.
32. Change encoder preference mid-recording: deferred to next session; current session unaffected; on next session start the preference is honoured (or downgraded with `encoder.fallbackEngaged`).
33. Change diagnostics verbosity: `engine.setLogLevel` called; helper log level changes within 1 s; new `engine.logLine` events reflect the new threshold.

**Diagnostics:**

34. "Copy diagnostics bundle" produces a zip containing: last 5 per-session JSON dumps, helper log tail, main log tail, redacted settings, environment manifest.
35. After a session loss, the corresponding `<sessionId>.json` exists in the diagnostics dir and is referenced by the `sessionLost` event's `diagnostics_path`.

**Process cleanup (v1.1.0 invariant):**

36. After quitting the app cleanly, no `cove-replay-engine`, `ffmpeg`, or `pactl` processes remain (ps grep test).
37. After force-killing the Electron main process, on next launch the orphan helper is either adopted (if alive) or cleaned up; no zombie ffmpeg.

**Recovery flow:**

38. After a helper crash with an active recording, on next launch the recovery banner appears; clicking Save invokes `replay.restoreRecoveredSession` → snapshot → export; the produced MP4 plays end-to-end.
39. Clicking Discard removes the recovered session from disk; next launch shows no banner.

## 25. Summary of the contract

- **Three processes, two IPC boundaries.** Renderer ↔ Main over Electron IPC; Main ↔ Helper over length-prefixed JSON-RPC on UDS / named pipe.
- **One method namespace** (`capture.*`, `replay.*`, `export.*` events, `encoder.*` events, `engine.*`) shared across both boundaries with snake_case on the wire and camelCase in the preload.
- **One renderer FSM** with explicit states bound to helper events. No timers ever drive transitions. `capture.sessionReady` is the only entry to `RECORDING`. `SAVING` does not freeze the HUD. `EXPORTING` is concurrent with `RECORDING`.
- **One supervisor.** Main spawns, monitors (passive heartbeat + child-exit event), restarts (3 attempts, exponential), and shuts down the helper. Helper owns ffmpeg / pipewire lifecycle entirely; main scrubs only the socket and PID files.
- **Issues #1 / #3 / #4 are structurally absorbed.** Region is a first-class settings mode with an app-owned overlay. `sessionReady` is the only path into `RECORDING`. Three separate clocks for session / replay window / export progress; never conflated.
- **Packaging** is `extraResources` per target with a sha256 sidecar per shipped artifact, per the global release rule.
- **Linux first; Windows path shape preserved** without locking macOS out.

This is what T-009 will write tests against and what the implementation tickets pick up.
